chunks: Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked him about wudu (ablution): how much water should a man pour over his right hand before putting it into the vessel? He said: once after the occurrence of urine, twice after feces, and three times after janabah.
And with this chain, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from ʿAli ibn al-Sindi, from Hammad ibn ʿIsa, from Hariz, from Abi Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
A man washes his hand once after sleep, twice after feces and urine, and three times after janabah.
As for what al-Husayn ibn Saʿid narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-ʿAlaʾ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who urinates and nothing touches his right hand: may he immerse it in the water? He said: Yes, even if he is junub.

So the correct understanding of this report is the lifting of prohibition from that, because that is among the etiquettes and not among the obligations. The obligation only applies when there is impurity on his hand that would spoil the water, and that which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.النَّجَاسَةٌ: ritual impurity present on the hand
key_terms.الْآدَابِ: recommended etiquettes or manners, not binding duties
key_terms.الْإِنَاءِ: the vessel containing water used for purification
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: janabah, the state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: feces; a state after relieving oneself that affects hand-washing etiquette
key_terms.الْوَاجِبَاتِ: obligatory acts that must be fulfilled
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: How many times should the hand be washed before placing it in the wudu vessel after urine, feces, sleep, or janabah?
ai.summary: These reports discuss the recommended washing of the hand before putting it into the water vessel during wudu (ablution), with differing counts depending on the state involved such as urine, feces, sleep, or janabah. The final passage clarifies that these counts are matters of etiquette rather than obligation, and that obligation applies only when actual najasah is present on the hand such that it would contaminate the water.
